answer: The orchard multiplier is published, charged in lagoon, and marble lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 15 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 1175 identities would post 2399 proofs and burn roughly 86 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
